title: Bin El Ouidane reservoir, 21 Aug to 2 Sep 2026
summary: From 21 Aug to 2 Sep 2026 the radar shows the lake shrinking from 30.63 km2 to 29.75 km2 while the land barely changed. Only 0.23 km2 turned brighter and 0.27 km2 darker in HV over the 12 days.

sections.heading: What changed
sections.text: The lake changed by -0.88 km2, or -2.9%. Mean HV rose by 0.1 dB and mean HH by 0.16 dB. In HH, 0.39 km2 turned brighter by more than 3 dB and 0.26 km2 darker.

sections.heading: Where, by terrain type
sections.text: Trees, shrub and rugged slopes had 0.09 km2 brighter and 0.1 km2 darker in HV. The small changing fields type lost 1.06 dB in HV on average, the largest change of any type, but it covers very little of the circle. Rough dry ground and fields had 0.05 km2 brighter and 0.05 km2 darker in HV.

sections.heading: Possible causes
sections.text: Possible cause for the lake: summer drawdown, with water released for irrigation and lost to evaporation; the dam's release record would confirm it. Possible cause for the changing fields: a harvest or ploughing, which removes the plants that scatter HV; a field visit would check it.

sections.heading: Limits
sections.text: Neither date carries a flag. Lake areas are approximate: 10.4% and 8.6% of the outline falls on land in the optical photo. One track only, so slopes facing away from the radar can fall in shadow.

sections.heading: What an agency could do next
sections.text: Compare the 0.88 km2 loss with the dam's release volumes for the same 12 days. Keep following the lake every 12 days to see whether the drawdown continues.
